title.narrative: Sustaining WASH (Water Sanitation and Hygiene) services accessed by the returning and vulnerable pop

description.narrative:
CAFOD in partnership with Kosti Pastoral Region and Upper Nile Rural Water Department intends to consolidate and sustain its work in the WASH (Water Sanitation and Hygiene) activities in 3 Payams of Maban County. The Payams are Bunj, Guffa and Jamam and the estimated population is around 15,000 .The thrust of this project is to 1) reinforce the capacities of the local communities and authorities to operate and maintain the existing water supply facilities in the County 2) promote behaviour change among the local population on hygiene and sanitation issues. The intended outcome of the project is improved public health status of the Maban people through undisrupted provision of portable water and population’s willingness to adopt new personal and environmental hygiene practices.
The main activities to be carried out include; 1) support the training of 20 new community handpump mechanics both men and women, 2) organise refresher training for the existing 18 community handpump mechanics 3)support the running of the 2 water yards in Jamam Payam 4) provide incentives to handpump mechanics following major repair work,5) support the training of 10 Community hygiene promoters on PHAST methodology 6) support the County Authorities to have the capacity to conduct regular water quality testing and establish a Flood/WASH Contingency Plan.
In order to promote behaviour change on personal and environmental hygiene, the project is going to carry out the following activities ; conduct a Knowledge Attitude and Practice (KAP) Survey in 3 densely populated locations of Jamam, Bunj and Kilo Ashara in order to establish a base line on the current situation, facilitate the training and work of 10 community hygiene promoters selected from 5 villages (Jamam, Bunj, Kidwa, Banjela and Nilla) on PHAST. PHAST stands for Participatory Hygiene and Sanitation Transformation. It is designed to promote hygiene behaviours, sanitation improvements and community management of water and sanitation facilities using specifically developed participatory techniques. The project will conclude with a post intervention KAP survey to establish the level of improvement or lack of it on hygiene and sanitation issues.
